主要讨论点：使用多台Mac组建集群进行AI模型推理的可行性与潜在问题

不同观点：
• 支持苹果集群的经济性
  - Mac集群能以较低成本提供大内存容量（如3TB RAM），适合运行超大规模模型（如1万亿参数的Kimi K2）
  - 对比NVIDIA方案：$50k的苹果集群可提供87%的GH200集群容量，但成本仅18%
  - 苹果供应链稳定，在显存市场混乱时可能成为性价比选择（@btown）

• 技术可行性争议
  - 硬件层面：
    - 雷电接口稳定性存疑，缺乏专业级互联方案（如QSFP）（@geerlingguy）
    - 机架部署困难（电源键位置/线缆管理问题）（@geerlingguy）
    - 与NVIDIA设备（如DGX Spark）的高速互联受限（@storus）
  - 软件层面：
    - macOS远程管理工具链不如Linux完善（如系统升级需GUI干预）（@geerlingguy）
    - 缺乏官方RDMA API支持（@jamesfmilne）

• 苹果潜在战略方向
  - 应开发基于M芯片的隐私优先AI云服务（@int32_64）
  - 需恢复可扩展的Mac Pro设计（@pjmlp）
  - 产能与数据中心扩展可能成为瓶颈（@zeristor）

补充讨论：
- 非ML分布式计算的应用可能性（@FridgeSeal）
- 社区技术突破（如George Hotz通过tinygrad实现Mac-NVIDIA混合方案）
- 消费级顾虑：M系列新品价格可能影响采用率（@irusensei）

争议焦点：
- 雷电接口是否适合长期作为集群互联方案
- macOS作为服务器系统的成熟度
- 苹果是否应优先发展专业级硬件而非消费级设备改造

主要讨论点：亚利桑那州是否适合建设AI数据中心，尤其是考虑到其水资源短缺问题。

不同观点：
• 支持建设AI数据中心的一方认为，亚利桑那州具备良好的基础设施和政策支持，能够吸引高科技投资。例如，该州气候干燥、土地成本较低，且政府对科技企业有税收优惠。
• 反对建设AI数据中心的一方则强调亚利桑那州的水资源短缺问题，认为大量数据中心会加剧当地的水资源危机。评论中有人提到，数据中心运行需要大量冷却用水，而这在干旱地区可能不可持续。
• 另一部分人持中立态度，认为虽然水资源是个问题，但可以通过技术手段（如使用空气冷却或回收水）来缓解影响，同时也能带动当地经济发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何在经济发展与环境保护之间取得平衡。一些人质疑是否有足够的政策保障来确保数据中心不会过度消耗水资源。
• 也有人提到其他州（如内华达州）同样面临干旱问题，但仍在积极发展数据中心，说明水资源问题并非不可克服的障碍。
• 讨论中还涉及亚利桑那州未来如何规划和管理水资源，以确保可持续发展。

data.title: Auto-grading decade-old Hacker News discussions with hindsight
data.author: __rito__
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者利用AI模型（如ChatGPT 5.1）对10年前Hacker News上的讨论进行回顾性评分和分析的项目。作者通过下载2015年12月的每日热门文章及其评论，使用AI模型生成分析报告，包括总结讨论内容、验证预测准确性、评选最具前瞻性或错误的评论，并对参与者进行评分。该项目旨在展示AI如何高效地分析历史数据，同时提醒人们未来AI可能持续审视当前行为。作者还分享了代码库和生成的静态网页，供其他人探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[评估历史评论的预测准确性及其方法论]

不同观点：
• **支持评估预测准确性**  
  - [modeless] 提出通过Chrome扩展对用户的预测准确性进行评分，并将准确性高的用户的投票权重提高。  
  - [Rperry2174] 认为“无聊但正确”的观点往往最准确，建议通过某种方式提前识别这些观点。  
  - [MBCook] 对评分结果感兴趣，并希望长期跟踪用户预测准确性的变化。  

• **质疑评估方法**  
  - [hackthemack] 指出LLM错误地将历史事实叙述误判为预测。  
  - [LeroyRaz] 批评LLM只是判断评论是否符合主流观点，而非真正评估预测准确性。  
  - [jacquesm] 强调预测需具备可证伪性，许多条目缺乏预测价值。  
  - [xpe] 认为项目在方法论和数据质量上存在严重缺陷，呼吁更严谨的研究态度。  

• **中立或幽默态度**  
  - [tptacek] 调侃评分结果的随机性，但对某些评论上榜表示开心。  
  - [pierrec] 幽默地接受低分评价。  
  - [nixpulvis] 表达对评分系统潜在滥用的担忧。  

补充讨论：  
- **争议焦点**：LLM是否真正评估了预测准确性，还是仅仅迎合主流观点（如 [LeroyRaz] vs. [modeless]）。  
- **方法论问题**：如何定义和验证预测（[jacquesm] 和 [xpe] 强调可证伪性和严谨性）。  
- **应用场景**：评分系统的潜在用途（如扩展工具、长期跟踪）与风险（如滥用或误导）。

46220540.article_content:
Auto-grading decade-old Hacker News discussions with hindsight
10 Dec, 2025
TLDR:
https://karpathy.ai/hncapsule/
Yesterday I stumbled on this HN thread
Show HN: Gemini Pro 3 hallucinates the HN front page 10 years from now
, where Gemini 3 was hallucinating the frontpage of 10 years from now. One of the comments struck me a bit more though - Bjartr linked to the
HN frontpage from exactly 10 years ago
, i.e. December 2015. I was reading through the discussions of 10 years ago and mentally grading them for prescience when I realized that an LLM might actually be a lot better at this task. I copy pasted one of the article+comment threads manually into ChatGPT 5.1 Thinking and it gave me a beautiful analysis of what people thought + what actually happened in retrospect, even better and significantly more detailed than what I was doing manually. I realized that this task is actually a really good fit for LLMs and I was looking for excuses to vibe code something with the newly released Opus 4.5, so I got to work. I'm going to get all the front pages of December (31 days, 30 articles per day), get ChatGPT 5.1 Thinking to do the analysis, and present everything in a nice way for historical reading.
There are two macro reasons for why I think the exercise is interesting more generally:
I believe it is quite possible and desirable to train your forward future predictor given training and effort.
I was reminded again of my tweets that said
"Be good, future LLMs are watching"
. You can take that in many directions, but here I want to focus on the idea that future LLMs
are
watching. Everything we do today might be scrutinized in great detail in the future because doing so will be "free". A lot of the ways people behave currently I think make an implicit "security by obscurity" assumption. But if intelligence really does become too cheap to meter, it will become possible to do a perfect reconstruction and synthesis of everything. LLMs are watching (or humans using them might be). Best to be good.
Vibe coding the actual project was relatively painless and took about 3 hours with Opus 4.5, with a few hickups but overall very impressive. The repository is on GitHub here:
karpathy/hn-time-capsule
. Here is the progression of what the code does:
Given a date, download the frontpage of 30 articles
For each article, download/parse the article itself and the full comment thread using Algolia API.
Package up everything into a markdown prompt asking for the analysis. Here is the prompt prefix I used:
The following is an article that appeared on Hacker News 10 years ago, and the discussion thread.
Let's use our benefit of hindsight now in 6 sections:
1. Give a brief summary of the article and the discussion thread.
2. What ended up happening to this topic? (research the topic briefly and write a summary)
3. Give out awards for "Most prescient" and "Most wrong" comments, considering what happened.
4. Mention any other fun or notable aspects of the article or discussion.
5. Give out grades to specific people for their comments, considering what happened.
6. At the end, give a final score (from 0-10) for how interesting this article and its retrospect analysis was.
As for the format of Section 5, use the header "Final grades" and follow it with simply an unordered list of people and their grades in the format of "name: grade (optional comment)". Here is an example:
Final grades
- speckx: A+ (excellent predictions on ...)
- tosh: A (correctly predicted this or that ...)
- keepamovin: A
- bgwalter: D
- fsflover: F (completely wrong on ...)
Your list may contain more people of course than just this toy example. Please follow the format exactly because I will be parsing it programmatically. The idea is that I will accumulate the grades for each account to identify the accounts that were over long periods of time the most prescient or the most wrong.
As for the format of Section 6, use the prefix "Article hindsight analysis interestingness score:" and then the score (0-10) as a number. Give high scores to articles/discussions that are prominent, notable, or interesting in retrospect. Give low scores in cases where few predictions are made, or the topic is very niche or obscure, or the discussion is not very interesting in retrospect.
Here is an example:
Article hindsight analysis interestingness score: 8
---
Submit prompt to GPT 5.1 Thinking via the OpenAI API
Collect and parse the results
Render the results into static HTML web pages for easy viewing
Host the html result pages on my website:
https://karpathy.ai/hncapsule/
Host all the intermediate results of the
data
directory if someone else would like to play. It's the file
data.zip
under the exact same url prefix (intentionally avoiding a direct link).
I spent a few hours browsing around and found it to be very interesting. A few example threads just for fun:
December 3 2015
Swift went open source
.
December 6 2015
Launch of Figma
December 11 2015
original announcement of OpenAI
:').
D

主要讨论点：[GPT-5.2的性能改进、用户体验、价格调整及与竞品的比较]

不同观点：
• **性能改进**  
  - 有用户认为GPT-5.2在推理能力上有所提升（如Extended NYT Connections benchmark的分数提高）。  
  - 但也有用户表示未感受到明显改进，认为其与GPT-5.1差异不大。  
  - 争议焦点：性能提升是否显著，以及是否值得价格上涨。

• **用户体验**  
  - 用户普遍批评现有模型的共同问题：过度自信的错误回答、不遵守指令、冗长回复、缺乏不确定性表达等。  
  - 部分用户赞赏GPT-5.2在代码生成和规划文档中的表现，认为其“更理智且可观察”。  
  - 争议焦点：用户体验是否因模型更新而改善，或仍存在根本性缺陷。

• **价格与价值**  
  - 用户注意到GPT-5.2的价格比GPT-5.1上涨40%，但对其新增功能（如40万token上下文窗口）表示认可。  
  - 部分用户认为竞品（如Gemini 3、Claude Code）在性价比上更具优势。  
  - 争议焦点：价格上涨是否合理，以及用户是否会转向竞品。

• **与竞品的比较**  
  - 用户提到Gemini 3在解决编程问题时表现突出，但批评其“无视指令”和输出质量不稳定。  
  - Claude Code被认为在代码生成领域具有竞争力。  
  - 争议焦点：OpenAI是否在竞争中落后，尤其是其不再与竞品直接对比的表现。

补充讨论：
- 用户建议针对不同任务使用独立会话，以避免模型混淆上下文。  
- 企业用户对OpenAI的稳定性、支持响应速度和功能缺失表示不满。  
- 部分用户对未来的硬件升级（如新数据中心）持乐观态度，认为可能带来更大突破。

  - 争议焦点：性能提升是否显著，以及是否值得价格上涨。

• **用户体验**  
  - 用户普遍批评现有模型的共同问题：过度自信的错误回答、不遵守指令、冗长回复、缺乏不确定性表达等。  
  - 部分用户赞赏GPT-5.2在代码生成和规划文档中的表现，认为其“更理智且可观察”。  
  - 争议焦点：用户体验是否因模型更新而改善，或仍存在根本性缺陷。

• **价格与价值**  
  - 用户注意到GPT-5.2的价格比GPT-5.1上涨40%，但对其新增功能（如40万token上下文窗口）表示认可。  
  - 部分用户认为竞品（如Gemini 3、Claude Code）在性价比上更具优势。  
  - 争议焦点：价格上涨是否合理，以及用户是否会转向竞品。

• **与竞品的比较**  
  - 用户提到Gemini 3在解决编程问题时表现突出，但批评其“无视指令”和输出质量不稳定。  
  - Claude Code被认为在代码生成领域具有竞争力。  
  - 争议焦点：OpenAI是否在竞争中落后，尤其是其不再与竞品直接对比的表现。

补充讨论：
- 用户建议针对不同任务使用独立会话，以避免模型混淆上下文。  
- 企业用户对OpenAI的稳定性、支持响应速度和功能缺失表示不满。  
- 部分用户对未来的硬件升级（如新数据中心）持乐观态度，认为可能带来更大突破。

  - cs702认为游戏是“labor of love”，建议支持开发者。

  - foxrider建议加入更多生物，如俄勒冈州的巨型蘑菇。

data.title: Fedora: Open-source repository for long-term digital preservation
data.author: cernocky
data.article_summary: Fedora是一款灵活、基于标准的开源存储软件，专为长期数字保存而设计。它适合图书馆、大学、博物馆等机构管理数字藏品，支持各种数字对象存储与语义关联。Fedora采用OCFL标准确保长期保存，拥有20多年历史，全球用户社区活跃。新版本Fedora 7.x即将发布，提供增强性能、可扩展性和集成能力。作为社区驱动软件，Fedora通过会员制获得资金支持，会员享有活动折扣等福利。提供下载、教程、文档等资源，鼓励用户加入社区共同发展。

Fedora is the flexible, standards-based, open-source repository software built to support long-term digital preservation.
Become a member

Why Choose Fedora?
Fedora is a sustainable open-source repository system underpinning many types of digital libraries and archives. It’s designed to store, manage, and preserve digital content. Fedora is particularly well-suited for institutions such as libraries, universities, research centres, and museums that need to preserve and provide access to their digital collections.
Flexibility
Fedora can store, preserve and provide access to any type of digital object. Through native support for semantic relationships, you are free to model your content to suit your needs and build out object relationships that are defined entirely by you.
Standards Based
Partnered with Fedora’s published API and the adoption of the OCFL standard for persistence, Fedora uses a variety of globally accepted standard web conventions for interacting with the application.
Global User Community
The Fedora program has been in existence for 20+ years, and our users represent an engaged, supportive and invested global community focused on sustainability and growth.

data.title: Rats Play DOOM
data.author: ano-ther
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个为老鼠设计的完整VR系统，用于让老鼠玩《毁灭战士》。系统包括运动追踪跑步球、全景头显、输入触发器和奖励电路，所有硬件和软件均为开源。从简易的初代版本（v1）升级到更先进的模块化版本（v2），改进了球体驱动机制、折叠式AMOLED屏幕（180°水平视野）、传感器和喂食系统。尽管设备功能完备，但因老鼠年龄限制未完成行为验证。硬件包含运动追踪球、定制触发器、全景屏幕和自动化奖励系统；软件采用模块化Python控制。项目旨在推动开源复制与改进。

46248323.article_content:
Intro
We built a complete VR setup from scratch to let rats play DOOM. The system includes a motion-tracked treadmill ball, a panoramic headset, an input trigger, and a reward circuit. All hardware and software components are open sourced, including 3D-printable designs, circuit diagrams, firmware, and control software.
The first version (v1) was built in New York by
Viktor
, who trained rats to walk through a corridor in DOOM using a simpler rig. That version was featured on Vice and PC Gamer. After moving back home, the project was paused. Public interest reignited development, leading to v2, a more advanced and modular version built in collaboration with electrical engineer
Sándor Makra
.
Akos Blaschek
later assisted significantly in documenting the project for open-sourcing, aiming to enable others to replicate and build upon this work. Key metallic components were designed and sourced in collaboration with
SZURWIN KFT
.
V1
Basic ball setup
Rats trained to run forward
Minimal sensors and mechanics
No panoramic screen
Rat VR Setup Version 1
V2
New ball driver mechanism for smoother movement
Foldable AMOLED screen with 180° horizontal and 80° vertical FOV, Full HD resolution
Upgraded sensors for movement tracking
Reinforced feeder system with mixing motor
Modular 3D-printable components
Improved electronics reliability and safety
Rat VR Setup Version 2
Full setup from side showing rat on ball, screen around, trigger, and water tube.
Limitations
We reached the point of rat habituation but didn’t start training. Our rats (Todd, Kojima, Gabe) aged out before full testing. The setup works, but behavioral validation is pending.
Hardware
The hardware is a comprehensive VR rig designed for rodents. It consists of a motion-tracked sphere that captures the rat's movements, a custom-built trigger for in-game actions, a curved panoramic screen for visual immersion, and an automated reward system that dispenses sugar water to reinforce behavior. All these components are mounted on a modular aluminum frame, creating a complete, self-contained environment for the rat to interact with the game.
View the Hardware Assembly Guide
Visual Interface
The headset wraps around the rat’s head with a foldable AMOLED screen. It maximizes immersion without obstructing whisker space. The screen supports Full HD resolution.
The headset frame also integrates several sensory components: two small air nozzles are positioned near the left and right whiskers, capable of delivering targeted air puffs on command (e.g., signaling wall collisions in-game). The frame provides a secure mounting point for the reward system's dispenser tube, placing it near the rat's mouth. Additionally, the design includes placeholders for miniature speakers near each ear, intended for future implementation of stereo audio cues.
Headset close-up.
3D Model: Headset
Locomotion
Movement is captured via a free-spinning ball under the rat. Rotary sensors track displacement and convert it into game motion. The ball can also be driven by motors.
These motors are used during training to roll the ball and simulate movement paths before a reward. This guides the rat on where to go, helping form movement-action associations. Like the trigger, this allows for programmatic training sequences with minimal initial input from the animal.
Ball mount showing driven/undriven modes and sensor placement.
3D Model: Stand/Ball
Trigger Input
The shooting input is a custom-built hand-operated lever. Rats pull it with their paws to fire. The lever is held in place by small springs, encased in a 3D-printed housing. It includes a rotary encoder to detect motion and a stepper motor to actuate it.
The motor allows programmatic control—pulling the lever to demonstrate shooting. This enables training by pairing visual cues with mechanical motion, reinforcing the association before the rat initiates the action on its own.
Close-up of trigger lever with encoder and motor.
3D Model: Trigger
Reward System
Positive in-game actions trigger a liquid reward: sugar water delivered through a precise dispensing mechanism. The system consists of:
Mixer: Continuously stirs the sugar solution to maintain even concentration
Pump + Pressure Sensor: Keeps the line under constant pressure
Solenoid Valve: Magnetic valve that opens to release exact 10 µL doses
Dispenser: Positioned near the mouth for easy access
This setup ensures accurate, repeatable reward delivery with minimal delay. The reward is synchronized with game events to reinforce desired behaviors.
The messy but functional reward circuit from behind.
Limitations
The current system assumes basic rat mobility and grooming behavior. Fine-tuning might be needed for rats of different sizes or temperaments. Trigger placement and reward tube flow may need calibration per subject.
Software
The setup is controlled through a modular Python system. The main entry point is
arena_scenario.py
, which runs the full control loop.
